cells.tense: You are here with the pen, holding more truths than one breath could carry.
cells.act: state the order of things once, without argument
cells.ask: Say the order of this once — what comes first, what follows — plainly, before anyone asks, then let it stand as said.
cells.core:
Several true things sit in your view at the same time, and the care in you is that none of them gets flattened. What you tend grows because its shape stays visible while it develops: you notice what is early, you don't force it forward, and your sight sits beside the growing instead of over it. That steadiness is already working through your hands.
What the balance is free to feed is a little more outward shape. So name it once, out loud or on paper, near the thing that is growing: here is what is true, here is the order of it. Say it without arguing for it, then stop there. A frame spoken plainly gives the shoot something to lean on, and gives you somewhere to stand while the rest keeps arriving.
cells.sheetLine: Said plainly, the order of it holds.

cells.tense: You will have decided how it turns out before it has had a chance to show you.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick one direction for these three days — not the truest, just the one — and steer by it until what you're tending shows something real.
cells.core:
Seeing several true things at once is meant to serve what's growing: you catch many possibilities, and because you catch them all, you can prepare for whichever one arrives. That is real strength, and it's why people bring you the hard cases.
Out on this edge, though, the many truths get laid over a future that hasn't happened, and the braced watching crowds the thing you're trying to help. So pick one direction and keep to it for three days. Not because the others are wrong — because steering needs a heading, and what you're tending needs someone at the wheel instead of a surveyor above it. After three days the seed will have said something, and you can look again.
cells.sheetLine: The seed can't show you while you hold every branch.

cells.tense: You knew a great deal once, and you have not come back to the room since.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Join one other person in the work this week and keep pace with them — no leading, no carrying it alone, just the two of you moving together.
cells.core:
The care is still in you, and clear knowing does not come the way it did. What you tend gets tended from a distance now, and you stand outside a room you used to be inside. That is where you are; nothing about why needs saying.
What brings the current back is company. Two people moving together carry more than one trying to start alone. So choose one person or one piece of work already in motion, and put yourself beside it rather than over it. Match their pace for a week, ask what happens at their end, and see what two people moving does that one can't manage alone. The clear knowing tends to come through the contact, not before it.
cells.sheetLine: Two streams moving carry what one won't.

cells.tense: You do the even-handed thing when nobody is looking and call it ordinary.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Once this week, do the thing your own sense of right points to — no announcement, nothing kept — and notice that you were the one deciding.
cells.core:
There is a clear sense in you of what is fair and what is owed, and it steers the small moments: who gets heard, what gets said, when to let something pass. That sense is yours. It works so quietly while you tend what grows that you have stopped counting it as anything you do — it just looks like how things go.
So this week, when that inner sense points to a move, make it plainly, and let one small act stand as your decision rather than as the obvious thing. Nothing needs to be said to anyone. The point isn't credit; it's noticing that you were the one choosing, and that what grows here grows because you keep choosing it.
cells.sheetLine: The even-handedness is yours, even unspoken.
